ThingDef.label: white petal
ThingDef.description:
The white petal is the humblest material in botany, and the starting point of every other colour. It can be ground into mana powder, dyed into a different colour, or condensed into pixie dust at an elven gate. It is not a building material, and it cannot be worn or sown.
Plucked, it still holds a little of the warmth the sun left in it - and then that is gone from between your fingers.

ThingDef.label: orange petal
ThingDef.description:
An orange petal is stock for colouring and grinding, and rarely goes into growing a flower. It is dyed from white petals, and can be ground into mana powder or condensed into pixie dust at an elven gate. It is not a building material.
A layer of colour pressed flat under the evening sun, its edges still letting light through.

ThingDef.label: yellow petal
ThingDef.description:
Yellow petals are spent on raising flowers rather than building with them - the daybloom is grown on them. They can also be ground into mana powder, or condensed into pixie dust at an elven gate. They are not a building material.
A yellow loud enough to be rude; set it in the dark and it is the first thing your eye is called to.

ThingDef.label: cyan petal
ThingDef.description:
Cyan petals are mostly spent on defensive flowers - the storm bloom is grown on them. They can also be ground into mana powder, or condensed into pixie dust at an elven gate. They are not a building material.
The colour of the sky a moment before the storm, cold enough to make you walk faster.

ThingDef.label: purple petal
ThingDef.description:
Purple petals are spent on the flowers that feed on people: the rosa arcana and the life orchid are both grown on them. They can also be ground into mana powder, or condensed into pixie dust at an elven gate. They are not a building material.
Purple so heavy it looks as though the night had been squeezed into the grain of the petal.

ThingDef.label: green petal
ThingDef.description:
Green petals are the main petal stock of the turret flowers: the blight eater, the thornbell, the blastcalyx and the ancient starfall bloom all want them. They can also be ground into mana powder, or condensed into pixie dust at an elven gate. They are not a building material.
It feels in the hand like a small piece of spring that never got round to hardening.

ThingDef.label: red petal
ThingDef.description:
Red petals go into the aggressive flowers - the bitter bloom and the thorn flower are both grown on them. They can also be ground into mana powder, or condensed into pixie dust at an elven gate. They are not a building material.
Red enough to feel hot in the hand, and up close there is a smell like rust.

ThingDef.label: black petal
ThingDef.description:
Black petals are spent on the flowers that work at night - the nightshade is grown on them. They can also be ground into mana powder, or condensed into pixie dust at an elven gate. They are not a building material.
Black enough to drink the light; only at the right angle does a thread of grain show.
